A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Prompt Injection as Role Confusion. All 30 pages, including Appendices A-K, equations, figures, and tables, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original jailbreak and agent-exfiltration experiments, role-probe measurements, ablations, and statistical analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including attack evaluations, role-perception analyses, and the appendix regression analysis.

M1.justification: CoT Forgery retains the same auxiliary-model generation and query-forgery concatenation procedure. The layer-wise linear role probes and their training procedure remain unchanged (Sections 3.1 and 4.1; Appendix G).

E1.justification: Both versions use StrongREJECT, Wikipedia exfiltration tasks, C4/Dolma3 probe-training data, and OASST1/TOXICCHAT conversations. The gardening, mistagging, and system-position scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains raw harmful queries and model-card standard-jailbreak rates as comparators. Figure 3 retains standard prompt injection versus CoT Forgery. The appendix comparison methods are unchanged.

E3.justification: Model configurations, sample counts, metrics, tagging conditions, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Section 3.3 replaces 'ReAct loop' with 'agent loop,' but Appendix B.2 retains the identical ReAct procedure.

E4.justification: The logic and style ablations, gardening case study, cross-model and layer analyses, template controls, and system-position experiment are unchanged (Appendices C-K). No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Figure 9 retains 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, and Table 3 retains template-clustered standard errors and p-values. Neither version changes seed information, repeated-run reporting, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Matched results remain unchanged throughout. Examples include the 60.5% versus 9.7% ASRs in Figure 4, the 2%-70% lowest-to-highest quantile results in Figure 10, and the Userness coefficient of 6.01 in Table 3.

T1.justification: The role and CoTness definitions in Section 4.1 and the mathematical probe formulation in Appendix G are unchanged. The added linear-projection caveat qualifies interpretation without introducing a formal result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that role confusion underlies prompt injection, introduce role probes and CoT Forgery, and predict attack success before generation. The revised emphasis on standard agent attacks and other spoofable cues reflects material already present in v1.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies representational equivalence as 'same up to overlapping linear projections' (Section 4.2, footnote 7). Section 7 also explicitly links longer system prompts losing priority to declining perceived Systemness, refining interpretation of the retained position analysis.

D1.justification: Appendices A, B, G, and J retain the same implementation details, auxiliary models, judging procedures, probe hyperparameters, and template information. Code and demo access remain redacted with instructions to contact the authors.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Andriushchenko and Flammarion (2025) and shortens the attack-survey discussion. Five earlier references, including Wei et al. (2023) and Qi et al. (2021), disappear. The overall mechanistic research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, contribution bullets are reordered, Section 4 is renamed, and numerous explanatory passages in Sections 4-7 are recast. This constitutes extensive narrative editing despite stable scientific content and appendix organization.

P2.justification: The same 32 figures and three tables are retained. Table 1 moves upward within page 6, Figure 8 moves to the top of page 7, and surrounding text reflows. The underlying displays, axes, legends, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The rewritten abstract and introduction more clearly connect the attacks, probes, and generalization experiments. The linear-projection qualification adds useful interpretive precision. These provide a modest gain despite reduced related-work context; experimental support and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
